task.title: Clip, mask and blend
task.shortdesc: You can show only a part of an element, fade it with a mask, and choose how it mixes with what is behind it.

info.p: A clip cuts away the parts of an element outside an area. Define the area with a clipPath element, and name it in the clip-path property of the element. The shapes inside the clipPath make the area: the parts of the element that are under them stay visible. The clip-rule property of a shape works as fill-rule does for the area it makes.

By default the numbers inside a clipPath are user units. With clipPathUnits="objectBoundingBox" they are fractions of the box of the clipped element, so the same clip fits elements of any size. A clip-path that names something that is not a clipPath clips nothing.

The clip-path property accepts basic shapes too: circle(), ellipse(), inset(), polygon() and path(). A word before or after the shape chooses the box the shape is measured in: fill-box is the box of the shape without its stroke, stroke-box includes the stroke, and view-box is the whole drawing.

stepxmp.pre: <defs> <clipPath id="disc"> <circle cx="55" cy="45" r="32"/> </clipPath> </defs> <rect x="10" y="10" width="90" height="70" fill="#cfe3f5" clip-path="url(#disc)"/>

step.cmd: Fade an element with a mask

info.p: A mask makes parts of an element transparent. Define it with a mask element, and name it in the mask property or attribute of the element. The children of the mask are drawn, and where they are light the element shows, and where they are dark it is transparent. The mask uses the luminance of the colors, with their opacity. With mask-type: alpha on the mask element, the mask uses only the opacity of what is drawn, and the colors do not matter.

A mask has a region, given by x, y, width and height, outside which the element is not shown. It is the box of the masked element made 10% larger on every side, as the initial values -10% and 120% say. The attribute maskUnits="userSpaceOnUse" gives them in user units. The attribute maskContentUnits="objectBoundingBox" makes the numbers of the children fractions of the box of the element. A mask that names nothing makes the element invisible.

stepxmp.pre: <defs> <linearGradient id="ramp"> <stop offset="0" stop-color="#ffffff"/> <stop offset="1" stop-color="#000000"/> </linearGradient> <mask id="fade-out"> <rect x="120" y="10" width="95" height="70" fill="url(#ramp)"/> </mask> </defs> <rect x="120" y="10" width="95" height="70" fill="#1d4f7a" mask="url(#fade-out)"/>

step.cmd: Blend an element with what is behind it

info.p: The mix-blend-mode property chooses how the colors of an element mix with the colors under it. The initial value is normal. The values such as multiply, screen, overlay, darken and difference are the blend modes of the PDF format. The property isolation: isolate on a group stops its children from blending with what is outside the group.

fig.title: A clip, a mask and a blend mode

image.alt: A light blue disc cut from a rectangle. A dark blue rectangle that fades from opaque on the left to transparent on the right. Two overlapping circles, blue and yellow, whose overlap is green.

stepxmp.pre: <circle cx="260" cy="45" r="28" fill="#6fc3e8"/> <circle cx="285" cy="45" r="28" fill="#f2d649" style="mix-blend-mode: multiply"/>

info.p: A group with an opacity below 1, a clip or a mask is isolated too.
